chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who swore an oath of abstention (ila') from his wife and had not yet consummated the marriage with her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no ila' until he consummates the marriage with her.' So he (peace be upon him) asked: 'Do you see if a man were to swear that he would not cohabit with his wife for two years or more than that, would that be considered ila'?'.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (often referring to Imam Ali or used generally for Imams)
key_terms.إِيلَاء: Solemn oath of abstention from conjugal relations
key_terms.يَبْنِ: To cohabit/live with (in the context of marriage)
key_terms.يَدْخُلْ بِهَا: To consummate the marriage (enter into her)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for the validity of Ila' (oath of abstention) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the specific legal institution of 'ila' (solemn oath of abstention) requires prior consummation of the marriage, distinguishing it from a general vow of non-cohabitation made before the couple has slept together. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the timeline for divorce proceedings and the husband's waiting period, ensuring that the oath's legal consequences only attach once the marital bond is fully actualized through physical intimacy.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was asked about a man who solemnly swore from his wife and did not sleep with her’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no solemn oath until he sleeps with her’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Do you not see that if a man were to oath that he would not make up with his wife for two years or more than that, would that be a solemn oath?’
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that once a man who was involved in 7/a’ (swearing) against his wife before going to bed with her, asked ’Amir al-Mu’minin. He (the Imam) said, ‘ 7/a’ (swearing) does not place until one goes to bed with his wife,’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘If a man swears not to go to bed with his wife for two years or more, can this be 7/a’ (swearing)?”’
